use_when: UI/network/storage interactions cannot be proven adequately with current tests
an agent needs controlled browser interaction
avoid_when: the task has no browser surface
existing project browser tests already prove the outcome
adding browser infrastructure would not close the actual capability gap

notes: Choose the smallest surface: Playwright Test for durable E2E regression coverage; Playwright CLI + Skills for many high-throughput coding-agent workflows; Playwright MCP for persistent/introspective browser-agent loops.
Do not install all three surfaces by default.

For MCP, current upstream standard usage is `npx @playwright/mcp@latest`; for CLI, current upstream documents `npm i -g @playwright/cli@latest`; for project E2E, current upstream documents `npm init playwright@latest`.
Re-check upstream before execution because package versions and host-specific integration commands evolve.

credentials: none for ordinary local browser automation
browser/session credentials only when the target application itself requires authentication
permissions: browser access to the target environment
filesystem/network permissions required by the selected Playwright surface only

checks: run one representative browser path that corresponds to the original acceptance/failure evidence
confirm the selected surface can observe the needed DOM/network/storage state
prefer a repeatable test artifact when the behavior should remain guarded

steps: remove the selected Playwright dependency or global CLI with the package manager that installed it
remove/disable the Playwright MCP entry if MCP was selected
revert generated test/config files that were created only for evaluation

warnings: Playwright MCP is not a security boundary.
Persistent browser profiles can retain authenticated state; scope them deliberately.
MCP is not automatically the best coding-agent interface when CLI+Skills or normal tests are sufficient.
